findings.finding: Draft underrepresented the connection between self-command and social obligations.
findings.action: Added a public-duties topic and a cooperation topic with an exact quotation.

findings.finding: Draft underrepresented the religious and cosmological premises of the advice.
findings.action: Added a fourth context topic, presenting providence as Marcus’s claim rather than reader assent.

findings.finding: Book 3 paragraph 2 contains historical death anecdotes, including an attribution concerning Socrates that needs separate source checking.
findings.action: No anecdote reproduced in the primer; source edition unchanged. No claim that historical accuracy of the edition has been audited.

findings.finding: Providence is a recurrent premise, but Marcus also considers alternative accounts of the universe. A simple providence-only gloss obscures that reasoning.
findings.action: Refined existing context topic to invite attention to the premises and alternative reasoning.

findings.finding: Acceptance and inward retreat coexist with helping, correcting errors, changing one’s mind, and avoiding further injury without hatred.
findings.action: Refined cooperation topic; did not equate acceptance with approval of wrongdoing.

findings.finding: The severe self-instructions include permission to return after failing; bodily sensation is distinguished from an added moral judgment.
findings.action: Added a short practice-after-failure topic with an exact quotation. Avoided claiming that physical pain or injury is unreal.

findings.finding: The notebook includes attributed quotations and borrowed sayings alongside self-address; treating every entry as Marcus’s direct voice would flatten its form.
findings.action: Expanded the existing structure topic without adding an unsupported chronology or independently certifying the attributions.

findings.finding: Accepting help and revising judgment are explicit parts of the practice; failure to act can also be unjust.
findings.action: Refined the existing cooperation topic to include receiving help rather than presenting self-command as solitary self-sufficiency.

findings.finding: Mortality, loss of fame, and changes of scale recur strongly and were underrepresented in the opening-focused draft.
findings.action: Added a reading prompt about changing scale, allowing readers to question as well as follow the comparisons.

findings.finding: The initial opening privileged Book 1 after the rest of the work had been reviewed.
findings.action: Rewrote the opening to introduce justice, change, cosmic premises, and permission to question those premises; retained an accessible one-entry starting point.

findings.finding: Social kinship coexists with authority and severe judgments. The primer should not turn the work into uniformly gentle modern advice.
findings.action: Qualified the public-duties topic and added a prompt contrasting caution about others’ circumstances with sweeping judgments.

findings.finding: Reading-advice topics overlapped after successive additions.
findings.action: Merged the moral-example guidance into careful attention; retained five distinct What to notice topics and the existing three exact quotes.
